does: Cuts sheets of warqa into long strips, puts a spoonful of filling at one end of each strip and folds the end over it again and again, corner to corner, into a small neat triangle, with the loose end sealed down with a dab of fat.
how: Keep the warqa under a damp cloth. Cut a sheet into strips as wide as a hand, and brush each strip lightly with melted butter.
Put a small spoonful of filling at one end, a little in from the corner.
Fold the corner over the filling to make a triangle, then fold the triangle over on itself along the strip, again and again, as one folds a flag.
Seal the last flap with a dab of butter and tuck it under.
Lay the triangles on a tray and cover them until they are fried.

cues.text: Each pastry is a neat triangle with no filling showing at the corners.
The sealed flap holds without sticking and the triangle is firm and flat.

mistakes.mistake: Overfilling, which splits the thin sheet and leaks in the oil.
Letting the strips dry out, so that they crack when folded.
mistakes.fix: Cut only a few at a time and keep the rest under a damp cloth.

variant_of.differs: Wrapping encloses a filling in a leaf, caul fat or a thin omelette. Here the wrapper is a paper-thin sheet cut in strips, and the filling is folded up in a series of triangle folds along the strip.
